Errors are reduced through direct electronic data transfer and automated materials scheduling and take-off. Drawing formats are consistent and engineered to ensure excellent layout using standard graphics symbols. Flexibility is maintained through the capability to easily customize referenced graphics symbol libraries and, in some cases, drawing arrangements.

## INTEGRATED MODELING SYSTEMS

The applications discussed in the previous section primarily use the basic graphics capabilities of CAD. Integrated modeling systems, however, make extensive use of graphics data bases. They are structured so that most of the data is collected in the process of constructing 3-D electronic plant models. Most of the engineering documents (e.g., drawings and data sheets) are extracted from the graphics models or automatically generated from the data bases.

## SYSTEMS ENGINEERING AND INSTRUMENT DESIGN

Many computer vendor data base systems are initialized during the system engineering design of the piping and instrumentation diagrams. Line or nomenclature lists and other reports can be extracted from this data. Data consistency checks are made throughout to ensure that the information is complete and accurate.

The data base is further expanded by instrument engineers and can then support the generation of instrument line lists and data sheets. It can be used to assign and track cabling between individual instruments, field junction boxes, and control room marshalling racks and can reference appropriate graphics elements for the generation of instrument loop diagrams. Exhibit 17-6 illustrates this process. This process requires about half the staff hours and much less graphics terminal time than previously required for manual development of CAD drawings.
